football_evidence.question: Can Notre Dame take away Miami’s big plays?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Miami, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.2 of the 2.3 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Notre Dame has the ball (big plays on the ground): Notre Dame’s offense turns 6.3% of its runs into explosive gains, and Miami’s defense gives up explosive gains on 3.2% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
When Miami has the ball (third down): Miami’s offense converts 58.4% of its third downs, and Notre Dame’s defense allows opponents to convert 43.5% of their third downs (FBS average 39.6%).

When Miami has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Miami’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 8.3% of its runs, and Notre Dame’s defense stops 18.1% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).
In his last two games (BYU and Navy), Carr averaged 6.4 yards per attempt, against 9.5 in his six games before that.
contradicting: When Notre Dame has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Notre Dame’s offense has allowed a sack on 2.2% of its dropbacks, and Miami’s defense sacks the quarterback on 7.5% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Miami has the ball (big plays on the ground): Miami’s offense turns 8.9% of its runs into explosive gains, and Notre Dame’s defense gives up explosive gains on 1.8% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When Notre Dame has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Notre Dame’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 11.8% of its runs, and Miami’s defense stops 14.2% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.5%).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Notre Dame’s pass defense No. 18 nationally and Miami’s No. 81.
quarterbacks: CJ Carr has completed 148 of 223 passes (66.4%) for 1,878 yards, 8.4 yards per attempt, 18 touchdowns and 1 interception in eight games for Notre Dame, and has been sacked on 2 of 225 dropbacks.
Noah Grubbs has completed 15 of 23 passes (65.2%) for 176 yards, 7.7 yards per attempt, 1 touchdown and no interceptions in four games for Notre Dame, and has been sacked on 0 of 23 dropbacks.
Darian Mensah has completed 188 of 234 passes (80.3%) for 2,448 yards, 10.5 yards per attempt, 25 touchdowns and 1 interception in eight games for Miami, and has been sacked on 9 of 243 dropbacks.
Luke Nickel has completed 14 of 19 passes (73.7%) for 193 yards, 10.2 yards per attempt, 3 touchdowns and 1 interception in three games for Miami, and has been sacked on 1 of 20 dropbacks.
